opportunities.title: North Korea's IP Slip: How Bitget's $387M Hack Became a Whodunit With Homework Due
opportunities.why_now: Bitget's CEO just publicly named North Korea using IP clues within hours of confirming the $387M breach, giving a rare real-time forensic trail to dissect.
opportunities.angle: Security-forensics breakdown: walk through the IP evidence, compare to Lazarus Group's known TTPs from prior hacks (Ronin, Bybit), and score how convincing the attribution actually is.

opportunities.title: Circle and Tether Froze the Bitget Hacker's Wallet. The Money Left Anyway.
opportunities.why_now: Same-day reporting shows issuers moved fast to freeze stablecoins tied to the heist, but most funds still escaped—a live case study in the real limits of centralized freeze powers.
opportunities.angle: 'Priced-in reality check' post: what freezing actually stops (and doesn't), with a timeline of the chase vs. the funds that got away.

opportunities.title: KelpDAO vs. LayerZero: The Lawsuit That Turns 'We Endorsed the Setup' Into a Liability Trap
opportunities.why_now: KelpDAO just filed suit claiming LayerZero endorsed the exact bridge configuration exploited for $292M, opening a new legal front for infrastructure-provider liability in DeFi.
opportunities.angle: Legal-meets-security explainer: precedent-setting angle on whether protocol 'endorsements' create actionable duty of care—relevant to every LST/bridge integration since.

opportunities.title: Your Old NFT Listings Are a Live Exploit: The Magic Eden Approval Bug Nobody Revoked
opportunities.why_now: Magic Eden just placed 3,832 NFTs into whitehat custody after discovering legacy payment-processor approvals left $5.7M exposed—a textbook 'forgotten permission' vulnerability.
opportunities.angle: Actionable security checklist: how to audit and revoke old marketplace approvals right now, framed around this specific exploit mechanism.

opportunities.title: AlphaFi Died From an Oracle Error. That's Not News to Anyone Who's Been Paying Attention.
opportunities.why_now: AlphaFi just wound down entirely after an oracle failure, even with Sui Foundation support stepping in—another entry in the long ledger of oracle-dependent protocols failing predictably.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition piece: line up AlphaFi against past oracle-failure collapses (Mango, Euler-adjacent incidents) to argue oracle risk is structurally unsolved, not a one-off.
